messages:
Emma (PM): kicking off a short sync on the smart routing + fallback PRD. goal = agree scope, acceptance criteria, and launch gates by EOD Fri. customer asks (finance startup, regulated) need region pinning + deterministic fallbacks. :eyes:
Raj (Eng): quick question — do we want routing policies defined as declarative rules or policy objects executed by the router? recommend declarative for UX, policy objects for advanced users.
Miguel (ML): from model compatibility side: we need a compatibility matrix so router knows which quant/variant is acceptable fallback. examples: 'gptx-8b-quant' compatible with 'gptx-8b-fp16' but not with 'gptx-4b'.
Yael (SRE): SLOs we must hit: 99.9% p99 latency within tier thresholds, and automatic circuit-breaker for repeated fallback loops. also need tracing hooks for postmortem.
Sophia (CS): customers want explicit SLA language for 'region pin' — if primary region fails, do they expect failover to another region or degrade to a lower tier in the same region? two different sales promises.
Emma (PM): propose scope split: MVP (Tier routing + simple fallback chain in-region), M1 (cross-region failover w/ opt-in), M2 (compatibility-aware variant substitution + routing rules UI). prioritize MVP for next release.
Raj (Eng): MVP tech notes: router config file example:
```
route: {
  priority: [tier1, tier2],
  fallback: [{type: "variant", allow_quantized: true}, {type: "region"}]
}
```
We can implement evaluator + ordered fallback. need compatibility API from ML team.
Miguel (ML): will deliver /v1/compatibility/{model} that returns compatible_variant_ids and confidence. default list + fallback score. ETA two sprints for basic list. edge case: live model upgrades change compatibility — router must revalidate cache TTL 5m.
Yael (SRE): acceptance criteria (MVP):
- automated policy evaluation runs within 5ms median per request
- fallback executed <= 1 extra hop 99% of time
- observability: per-request route decisions logged and sampleable
- rollback: can disable fallback globally via feature flag
Raj (Eng): implementation considerations: atomicity of KV cache updates, avoidance of thundering herd when fallback triggers, and safe defaults so we don't send PII to unintended region.
Sophia (CS): customer-driven asks to track in PRD:
- region pinning per-tenant (opt-in)
- explicit consent + audit logs for cross-region failover
- per-tenant fallback blacklist (e.g., disallow lower-quality variants)
Emma (PM): launch gates for MVP:
- Feature complete + doc + samples (devex)
- Load test: simulated traffic with 2% forced primary failure
- Compliance review for cross-region behavior
- At least one pilot customer signed off on behavior
Raj (Eng): prioritization notes: big infra effort for cross-region; recommend taking M1 only for enterprise contracts. MVP should be 60% infra + 40% product/ML work approx.
Miguel (ML): edge cases to enumerate in PRD:
- model variant unavailable but compatible variant also degraded
- TTL mismatch between compat API and router cache -> stale fallbacks
- tokenization differences across variants -> subtle quality regressions
Emma (PM): I'll draft the PRD section tonight. ask: can Eng + ML owners comment inline by tomorrow morning? I'll add acceptance criteria above to the PRD.
Raj (Eng): can do. I'll add implementation risks and a small sequence diagram.
Yael (SRE): I'll add runbook snippets and an automated rollback playbook (deploy-bot will test).
Sophia (CS): I'll prepare a customer-facing FAQ and coordinate a pilot.
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled to staging for routing-v0 on 1763213000. :white_check_mark:
Emma (PM): great. final quick decision: MVP includes per-tenant region pinning read-only config (no UI) + router-level fallback chain limited to 2 hops. sound good?
Raj (Eng): agree.
Miguel (ML): agree, but flag tokenization QA for the pilot.
Yael (SRE): agree, will run canary with 10% traffic.
Sophia (CS): agree. I'll reach out to pilot customer.
Emma (PM): thanks all — I'll post PRD link here when done. :rocket:
